location_note: Western Wall Tunnels, c. 50 m west of the Temple Mount and west of Wilson's Arch, Old City of Jerusalem; no map reference. Placed by name (Jerusalem, Z4).
notes: 2018 probe inside vaulted Tunnel 230, which is built into the core of the dam wall (W5006) across the Tyropoeon Valley; the dam was exposed in Onn's 2007-2012 excavations and is coded here because the reported probe was dug inside it (choice C3). The stepped pool identified as a miqveh in Room 21 and the two Byzantine industrial pools are described from Onn's excavations; cited, not coded. Tunnel 230 itself (a built vault of undefined use) not coded. The tile stamp is the subject.

features.subtype: dam wall (width 14 m, length >100 m) across the Tyropoeon Valley, with vaulted tunnels 230 and 240 in its core
features.period: probably King Herod's reign or slightly later (Herod to early 1st c. CE)
features.quote: a wide dam wall built across the Tyropoeon Valley
